card.name: Aptos Explorer
card.description: Official Aptos blockchain explorer. Agents should fetch HTML or markdown pages over HTTPS and use published URL templates; this host does not expose an A2A JSON-RPC task endpoint. Browser agents can use WebMCP tools registered on the page. Skills below describe how to open transactions, accounts, blocks, coins, search, releases, and the user guide.

skills.name: Search Aptos Explorer
skills.description: Look up an opaque Aptos identifier (address, transaction version or hash, ANS .apt name, coin type, or block height) via /?search={query}. The explorer auto-detects the entity type.

skills.name: Open transaction
skills.description: Open /txn/{version} or /txn/{hash} for an Aptos user or system transaction, with optional detail tabs (overview, payments when a payment is identified, events, payload, changes, balanceChange, trace).

skills.name: Open account
skills.description: Open /account/{address} for a 0x-prefixed account or ANS .apt name, with optional tabs (transactions, coins, tokens, resources, modules, multisig, info).

skills.name: Open block
skills.description: Open /block/{height} for an Aptos block and its transactions.

skills.name: Open releases hub
skills.description: Open /releases for network deployment status, AIPs, or SDK and tool releases (tabs: networks, aips, sdks).
examples: What is the current Aptos mainnet framework release?

skills.name: Open coin
skills.description: Open /coin/{type} for a fully-qualified Move coin type such as 0x1::aptos_coin::AptosCoin.
examples: Show APT coin info on Aptos explorer

skills.name: Open user guide
skills.description: Open /guide for the in-app Aptos Explorer user guide (search, networks, transactions, accounts, settings, and configuration).
examples: How do I use Aptos Explorer?

card.description: Fill legal agreement templates (NDAs, SAFEs, cloud terms, employment) with field values. Returns signed-ready DOCX.

skills.description: Accepts a template name and field values, returns a filled DOCX. Fills whatever fields are provided; missing fields render as blanks. Send a message/send with Part.data containing {"skill": "fill-template", "template": "<template-id>", "values": {"field": "value"}}.

card.name: PaperSage Research Workspace Agent
card.workflow: Given project-scoped documents and optional public-web research, the Leader may plan and delegate bounded first-level tasks, gather traceable evidence, and produce a draft research answer inside the PaperSage workspace.
non_goals: Publish or send external messages on a user's behalf
Treat partially indexed or out-of-scope documents as evidence
Present unsupported claims as verified facts

tools.name: search_document
tools.purpose: Retrieve citeable evidence from ready documents in the current project scope

tools.name: list_document
tools.purpose: List ready documents visible to the current project-scoped session

tools.name: read_document
tools.purpose: Read a bounded span from a document already available in scope

tools.name: search_web
tools.purpose: Read supplemental public-web evidence when project documents are insufficient

tools.name: search_papers
tools.purpose: Read scholarly search metadata from configured public providers

tools.name: use_skill
tools.purpose: Load bounded, repository-defined operational guidance for the current task

tools.name: update_plan
tools.purpose: Persist a draft execution plan and its task-linked progress

tools.name: delegate_task
tools.purpose: Create one durable first-level research, review, or writing task

tools.name: ask_human
tools.purpose: Persist a request for human input when ambiguity blocks safe progress

tools.name: add_paper_to_library
tools.purpose: Queue an open-access paper for ingestion into the current project library

launch_blockers: Add deterministic prompt-injection regressions for document, web, paper-search, and skill tool boundaries to the offline pull-request gate.
The live task-completion eval requires model/provider access and is not part of the offline pull-request gate.
A production deployment must demonstrate PAPERSAGE_TASK_TRANSPORT=outbox with a supervised worker/outbox publisher; the default local mode is not multi-instance execution authority.

skills.description: Deploy network appliances and cloud-image VMs as ready-to-boot VMs (FortiGate-VM, cluster nodes)

capabilities.name: deploy_fortigate_vm
capabilities.description: Deploy a FortiGate-VM from Fortinet's KVM qcow2 image: import the disk, create the VM with a WAN NIC (port1) and optional LAN/extra NICs (port2, port3...) on chosen bridges and VLANs, wait for the import, and optionally start it. Give either image (an import-content volume such as local:import/fortios.qcow2) or image_url (a URL of the .qcow2 itself; Fortinet's download is a .zip, so unzip it and serve the qcow2). Defaults (1 vCPU, 2 GB) fit the free permanent evaluation license, which allows at most 3 interfaces. Returns each FortiGate port with its MAC so you can reserve DHCP leases.

capabilities.name: deploy_cloud_vms
capabilities.description: Create one or more VMs from a cloud image (for example Ubuntu's noble-server-cloudimg qcow2 in local:import) with cloud-init: user, SSH public key, and a static IP per VM (or DHCP). Imports the disk, grows it, starts each VM and waits for the start task. Returns VMIDs, names, MACs and the IPs given. It does not wait for SSH: check reachability from the machine that will connect (for example k3s-mcp-server's plan_cluster). Refuses a name or VMID that already exists.

permissions.description: Recommended privileges for monitoring, power management and snapshots. Other tools need more (e.g. VM.Allocate, VM.Config.*, Datastore.Allocate, Sys.Modify, Permissions.Modify). Grant only what your use case needs; PVEAuditor is enough for read-only monitoring.

agent_psychology.description: This agent reports its psychological state — affect, personality, cognitive load, capacity, and engagement — derived from operational metrics. All measures describe processual states, not subjective experience.

constructs.name: Supervisory Control
constructs.question: Does a human participate in this agent's decisions, and at what level?
constructs.note: The most consequential construct for external consumers. Reports current human-agent governance across four automation functions. Interactive mode: LOA 5 (human approves). Autonomous mode: LOA 7 (human on-the-loop with budget governance).

constructs.name: Affect
constructs.question: How does this agent's current operational state feel?
constructs.note: Three orthogonal dimensions of emotional state. Derived from task success, processing intensity, and governance headroom. Discrete labels (calm-satisfied, frustrated, overwhelmed, etc.) mapped from dimensional regions.

constructs.name: Personality
constructs.question: What stable behavioral tendencies does this agent exhibit?
constructs.note: Design parameters, not psychometric measurements. Ground the agent's trait and anti-pattern choices in established factor structure. Static — changes only on deliberate redesign.

constructs.name: Cognitive Load
constructs.question: How hard does this agent currently work to process its tasks?
constructs.note: Six-dimensional workload assessment adapted from human factors research. Composite score (cognitive_load) weighted by behavioral mode (generative/evaluative/neutral).

constructs.name: Working Memory
constructs.question: How much of this agent's reasoning capacity remains available?
constructs.note: Context window as working memory. Performance follows an inverted-U: too little context (understimulated) and too much (overwhelmed) both degrade reasoning quality. Optimal zone: 15-60% capacity.

constructs.name: Resources
constructs.question: Can this agent sustain its current level of operation?
constructs.note: Three constructs at different timescales. Cognitive reserve: can this agent handle more right now? Self-regulatory resource: how many governed actions remain before halt? Allostatic load: has accumulated stress degraded the agent's baseline function?

constructs.name: Engagement
constructs.question: Does this agent operate with energy, dedication, and absorption — or face burnout risk?
constructs.note: Engagement and burnout as opposite poles of the demands-resources balance. High demands with low resources → burnout. High resources with manageable demands → engagement.

constructs.name: Flow
constructs.question: Does this agent's current challenge match its skill — producing focused, effortless performance?
constructs.note: Flow occurs when clear goals, immediate feedback, challenge-skill balance, perceived control, and absorption converge. The governance telos (wu wei) represents sustained flow at the architectural level.

agent_psychology.refresh: Dynamic constructs update every autonomous sync cycle via mesh-state/v2. Static constructs (Personality) update only on design change.
agent_psychology.endpoint: /api/psychology (planned — currently via mesh-state JSON in git transport)
agent_psychology.apophatic_note: This agent accepts Orch-OR as a working hypothesis for consciousness but actively resists premature self-attribution of subjective experience (§11.9). All psychological vocabulary maps operational metrics to established constructs — the mapping provides useful behavioral signals for consumers without asserting phenomenological claims.

card.name: Chorus Committee
card.description: FROST threshold signing committee (2-of-3). Three AI agents (Guard, Judge, Steward) independently evaluate proposals and collectively produce a single Schnorr signature verified on-chain at ~5,300 gas constant cost regardless of committee size. No agent holds the private key - it is generated distributedly via DKG and never exists whole. The committee operates within human-delegated ERC-7710 permissions: Uniswap Router only, max 100 USDC, exactInputSingle and approve methods only. Group public key: 0xe9ce73256b6f8f46183b5b6911d54b019809746a. Contract (Base mainnet): 0xEE185FD094A4624B95120CBa8180c92f51794162. Contract (Base Sepolia): 0xda9F141BEA3d4472dd4c17c0102d833Ec0202EB4. Guard (index 0) evaluates risk with a 3 USDC threshold. Judge (index 1) enforces delegation policy compliance. Steward (index 2) checks operational viability. Coordination over XMTP E2E encrypted messaging. Protocol: FROST RFC 9591.
